column1: # Finding annotations — the JUDGEMENT layer of the audit, kept as data.
# Evidence lives in docs/audit/data/ and is machine-generated. Severity class,
# depth and epic ownership are calls a person makes, so they live here where
# they can be reviewed and argued with, instead of being buried in a generator.
# tools/audit/rank.php joins the two and renders docs/audit/GAPS.md, which is
# class         S0 silent wrong answer   (compiles, runs, answers differently than php)
#               S1 runtime hard failure  (crash / uncaught / stub that explodes later)
#               S2 compile or link hard failure, or a compiler crash
#               S3 static finding with no observed runtime effect
# tier          lowest ladder tier that hits it (1-8); 0 = compiler-intrinsic, hits everything
# depth         compiler-root | repr | prelude | stdlib-leaf | parser
# packages      distinct vendor packages affected (count, from the evidence files)
# epic          which follow-on epic owns it
# evidence      file under docs/audit/ backing the row

column8: title
strstr/strchr/strrchr resolved to the raw C bindings and returned a pointer where PHP returns a string — global PHP-semantics implementations now win at resolveCallName
strcmp/strncmp/strcasecmp/strncasecmp compared NUL-terminated, so strcmp("a\0b","a\0c") answered 0 — now length-aware, unsigned, with PHP's prefix rule

an erased local passed to a by-ref callee that appends a foreign kind stayed vec[unknown] — collectByRefWidenArgs skipped UNKNOWN, deferring to an INTRA-procedural scan that cannot see the callee's store

the widen scan walked CALL args only, so a `use (&$erased)` capture was an invisible by-ref writer; it now walks Closure_ captures too, and an append whose provenance is not visible at the site (a closure own param, supplied by the invoker) widens an erased element rather than being given the benefit of the doubt
no named group ever reached $matches in preg_match or preg_match_all — PCRE2's name table was never read; pcre2_pattern_info is now bound and the name is interleaved ahead of its number, as php does
preg_match ignored $flags entirely; PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE and PREG_UNMATCHED_AS_NULL now behave (preg_match_all already handled OFFSET_CAPTURE — the original finding conflated the two functions)

lowerTypeHint sent every hint containing `|` to a cell, so the union spelling of a nullable (`S|null`, identical to `?S` in php) lost its class — the static type became bare `object` and every dispatch keyed on it misfired. Not prelude-specific: prelude/reflection.php just happens to spell all four optional returns that way

the queue ran only from an atexit hook, so it fired AFTER main returned and after every trailing release had run its destructors; and register_shutdown_function dropped its ...$args, so a callback parameter read an unbound slot

MISNAMED, and the name cost the time: the two foreach loops were always correct and match the interpreter byte for byte. Splitting the probe into one statement per file put the SIGBUS on iterator_to_array, which routed every non-array argument into a \Generator-typed funnel — so an IteratorAggregate was read as a generator frame, its refcount taken for the state word and its class DESCRIPTOR pointer loaded from slot 0 and called, jumping into a read-only data page. The title was inherited from a memory note about a different crash and never bisected; the recorded evidence was rc>128 with an empty stdout, which says nothing about WHERE, because the harness block-buffers to a file and a fatal signal discards the buffer

found by the same probe's last line: `$bag instanceof Traversable` was false for a class implementing IteratorAggregate. classIsA matches a target against a class's OWN interface list and then walks parents, but Iterator and IteratorAggregate are built-ins absent from the class table, so the walk never reached their implicit base. php forbids implementing Traversable directly, so those two are the whole membership rule — modelled the way Stringable already was

the parser consumed the path operand and returned Expr::null, so `$x = require 'config.php'` was always null. Whole-program AOT already compiles the target's declarations in and already runs its top-level statements inline, so the LOAD was genuinely redundant — the VALUE was not. Each non-entry file's top-level `return` now stores into a per-file global instead of being dropped, and require/include resolves a path to that slot through a strcmp chain over the closed file set, comparing REALPATHs so the several spellings a program reaches one file by all match. No execution-order change: this is the eager model, chosen over lazy per-file units precisely because it does not move when any vendor file's top-level code runs. ⚠ The slot name was first derived from sha1(path) and that SEGFAULTED under self-host only: sha1 routes through OpenSSL EVP and link_stubs.sh stubs EVP_sha1 to `return 0` when linking the self-hosted compiler, so inside it every path hashed to one string and every file shared one slot. Derived from the source index instead — no hash. The normal suite stayed green throughout; only the fixpoint gate saw it

a REPEAT require_once/include_once returns php's bool(true); under the eager model every file's top-level code has already run inline, so nothing tracks that a unit was entered twice and the repeat re-reads the value slot instead. Bounded: the value is the same one, so only the true-vs-value distinction diverges. Closing it needs the lazy per-file unit model with a _once guard, which changes when every file's top-level code runs and wants its own worktree and a full gate

a file WRITTEN AT RUNTIME and then required can never work ahead of time — it is not one of the program's compile units, and no amount of path resolution changes that. Recorded rather than dropped because the original probe was written that way (file_put_contents then require) and a row that vanishes is indistinguishable from one never written. The probe was replaced with build-time-present fixtures keeping both real-world shapes: a file returning an array and a file returning a closure

PARTIAL: spl_autoload_register/unregister/functions now exist (prelude/autoload.php), so composer ClassLoader::register() compiles and registers instead of being a hard compile error. class_exists($n, true) still does not DRAIN the queue: the lookup is an emit-time fold into a static table and the guard machinery depends on it staying constant-foldable, so firing it is a design call. Bounded impact — ahead of time an autoloader can never define a class, so only the callback side effects are lost

the finding said absent; measuring said worse. func_num_args() was CONSTANT-FOLDED to the declared parameter count, so a three-optional function answered 3 for every call including the zero-argument one, and func_get_arg($i) with a non-literal index (the idiomatic loop) fell through to an undefined symbol. The count now rides a demand-gated side channel: the call site pushes what the SOURCE wrote before defaultFillArgs pads it, and the callee takes it in its first statement. Not a hidden parameter — the closure struct is fixed-arity and an indirect call could not carry one. Arguments written past the declared list ride a companion slot, which is what SymfonyStyle::comment() needs when it declares one parameter and reads func_get_arg(1)

closed by the main merge (prelude sapi.php + session.php + ob.php) plus putenv and php_sapi_name here — header/header_remove/headers_sent/headers_list/http_response_code/setcookie/setrawcookie, the session_* family, the ob_* family and the error-handler family all exist and were re-verified by CALLING them, not by asking after them. Only php WARNINGS differ (headers already sent), which is the north-star no-warnings divergence and not a gap in this surface

function_exists('<literal>') answered FALSE for 23 names that plainly work — the whole header/session/ob/error-handler surface. functionIsKnown consulted what the prelude HAD declared, but the prelude is demand-gated on a mention that looks like use, and a name appearing only inside function_exists deliberately does not create demand: the predicate was measuring its own gate rather than the language. It now also consults what the prelude WOULD declare, a hardcoded set that calibrate.sh derives from prelude/*.php and fails on drift. Safe in the direction that matters — a program that goes on to CALL the name makes a real mention, which injects the file

putenv now a codegen builtin over libc setenv/unsetenv. No shadow table, and that is why it round-trips: getenv reads the real environ and $_SERVER/$_ENV are built from it, so one store is visible to all three. setenv/unsetenv rather than C putenv, which takes ownership of a buffer this compiler will free. The name must be copied into its own NUL-terminated buffer — splitting in place by writing over the = is what C does and is UB here, because the argument is usually a string LITERAL, so LLVM kept the original bytes and setenv got NAME=value as the name, which is EINVAL: putenv answered false and set nothing

NEARLY CLOSED: was 44 of 53 common functions answering false; now 5. Fixed by teaching functionIsKnown the codegen builtins, the rest of the emitBuiltin dispatch and the compiler rewrites. The 5 left are DEMAND-GATED prelude names (error_reporting, register_shutdown_function, set_error_handler, ob_start, ob_get_clean) that the program only MENTIONS inside function_exists without calling — the prelude is then never injected. Measuring caught an over-inclusion too: `print` is a construct php does not expose, so claiming it exists was a regression of its own

array_walk_recursive handed its callback values that read back as raw bits — a witness of erased-byref-closure-capture, closed with it; array_push into an erased local was the same bug and is closed too
closed on main by cf74105 (`and`/`or`/`xor`), not by this branch — re-verified byte-exact after the merge

PARTIAL: `fn &()` / `function &()` now PARSE and carry returnsByRef; lowering refuses them with a precise message instead of compiling silently wrong code. Shipping the parse alone was measured and rejected — the alias came back a COPY, so $r = &$f(); $r[] = x left the original untouched. The missing half is the closure ABI, not the parser: named functions and methods already return by reference correctly

PARTIAL: a reference inside an array literal now PARSES and carries byRef; lowering refuses it with a message that names the construct, replacing an "unexpected token: Ampersand" that pointed at a character and explained nothing. It is NOT honoured, and shipping the parse alone was rejected on the fn-by-ref precedent: an element that aliases is a property of the SLOT, and there is nowhere to record one. ARRAY_REPR_* (bits 1-3) and ARRAY_ELEM_HINT_* (bits 4-6) are WHOLE-ARRAY flags, and RefAddr_ binds a LOCAL to a slot address, never a slot to a source - the same missing fact behind vardump-ref-marker. polyfill-deepclone builds an alias pool it later writes back through, so a copy would silently lose every write. Closing it properly means a REF cell tag pointing at a {rc,value} box, the widen-to-cell machinery already on this branch to promote any ref-taken array element channel, and ~50 element-access emit sites learning to deref - its own worktree and a full gate. The parse-blocked skip in gen_manifest.php therefore STAYS, with its reason upgraded from a parse error to a named refusal

a reserved word may name a class constant or an enum case in php; the lexer emits Keyword and the parser demanded Identifier. expectMemberName() accepts both, and only in member position — `class array` stays a syntax error
two halves: isIdentStart admitted ASCII only (php grammar is [a-zA-Z_\x80-\xff]), and once parsed the raw bytes reached the LLVM symbol — mangle/sanitizeSym now hex-escape any byte >= 0x80
same root as parser-reserved-enum-case — the const-name positions demanded Identifier where php allows a reserved word
ReflectionParameter::getAttributes absent; DI autowiring and controller argument resolution cannot work
ReflectionParameter::getDefaultValue/getDeclaringClass absent
no ReflectionUnionType / ReflectionIntersectionType
ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF is declared but the filter matches exact names only
ReflectionEnum absent; doctrine enum types and form choices need it
newInstanceWithoutConstructor absent; doctrine hydration and var-exporter need it
a whole-array $GLOBALS read is a hard compile error
no PDO, PDOStatement, PDOException or sqlite binding exists at all

PARTIAL: the 10 missing SPL EXCEPTIONS are declared with php parentage (BadMethodCall/Domain/Length/BadFunctionCall under LogicException; OutOfBounds/Overflow/Range/Underflow/UnexpectedValue under RuntimeException; JsonException under Exception). Still absent: the SPL ITERATORS and DirectoryIterator/DOMDocument/ReflectionExtension
$_GET/$_POST/$_COOKIE/$_FILES/$_REQUEST are always []; $_SERVER carries a CLI shape with no web keys
the analyzer does not model `use function Ns\name` imports; 10 sites, code compiles and runs

preg_match $matches had to become cell-element so PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE can hold its [text,offset] pairs; measured 0.088s -> 0.102s (+16%) on a 300k-iteration match loop. Recoverable by specializing on a constant $flags argument, which is compiler work, not stdlib work

var_dump does not mark a slot that IS a reference: php prints &int(99) for $a[1] after $r = &$a[1], manticore prints int(99). The ALIAS itself is correct — the value changes through the reference — so this is a display divergence, but it is the same missing fact (which slot is a reference) that a `[&$a[$k], $v]` literal would have to preserve, which is why parser-ref-in-array-literal is not just a parser gap

a non-literal argument folded to false for EVERY function, builtins included — a loop over names reported strlen, count and floor all missing, which is what made this audit's own SAPI presence probe claim trigger_error was absent. The set is CLOSED at compile time, so it is now a lookup: LowerFromAst assembles the candidate universe (fnDecls, bare aliases, RESOLVED_FNS, Analyze\Builtins::functionNames, the emitter-inline list, the prelude-provided list) and runs EVERY candidate through functionIsKnown — the same predicate the literal fold uses, so the two forms cannot disagree by construction. Emitted as a flat name table plus a scan rather than an unrolled strcmp chain: ~1000 names, and one presence check is not worth a thousand basic blocks. Demand-gated, so a program that never asks dynamically pays nothing. ⚠ the names must be interned BEFORE the string pool renders, exactly like the global initialisers above it

three cases diverge from php on LINUX but match byte-for-byte on macOS: runtime_env, ini_session_defaults, string_gaps. None of them touch anything this session added — they were simply never seen, because difftest had never been run on this branch on either platform. Pre-existing and platform-specific, which per the standing rule (a tier whose finding set differs across platforms is itself a finding) is exactly the class that must not be left implicit

difftest flags error_handler_basic and trigger_deprecation_shape, and both are pure diagnostic FORMAT: php CLI emits every notice TWICE (once prefixed `PHP Notice:  `, once `Notice: `) and names the file by ABSOLUTE path, while manticore emits once with the path as written. The suite passes because its expected files encode our shape; only raw php parity sees it. Pre-existing, and adjacent to the no-warnings-throw-exceptions north star rather than a bug under it

a compiler-side dependency on any symbol that link_stubs.sh stubs is invisible everywhere except the self-hosted build. sha1() was the instance (EVP_sha1 -> return 0), and the failure mode was a SEGFAULT in a compiled program, several removes from the cause. 43 symbols are stubbed in a self-host link — the crypto family, iconv, pcre2 and the fiber asm among them — and the compiler must not depend on ANY of them for a decision it bakes into output. A scan of src/ outside Runtime/Stdlib found no other use

MISDIAGNOSED as a ??= gap. `??=` was always fine; the blocker was PRECEDENCE. php puts a full expression on the right of `??`, and assignment is an expression, so `$d = self::$d ?? self::$d = require …` parses as `$d = (self::$d ?? (self::$d = …))`. parseNullCoalesce recursed into ITSELF for the right operand, which stops below `=`, so the `=` was left for the caller and the whole coalesce became an assignment TARGET — hence the misleading `unsupported assign target kind NullCoalesce`. Right operand now parses at parseAssign level (NOT parseExpression: and/or/xor bind looser, so `$a ?? $b and $c` must stay `($a ?? $b) and $c`). Blocked T1 through polyfill-intl-icu, and needs the include-value work to be useful, since the idiom memoises a `require`

an assignment is an EXPRESSION whose value is the value ASSIGNED, and the store emitters returned the slot's STORAGE ENCODING instead. Where the slot NaN-boxes, the boxed word escaped as the expression value while the node's type still said string/int, so a consumer inttoptr'd a tagged word and dereferenced it. The recorded repro was MIS-DECLARED and measuring corrected it: `public static string $d` never crashed, because a concrete hint does not box. It is the UNHINTED and `mixed` declarations that fault, and the same bug rode the INSTANCE-property store (`$v = ($o->mixedProp = 'x')`), which the finding never named. It was not only a crash either — through an int slot it was a silent wrong answer, `$v = (M::$i = 42)` reading -4222124650659798. Both emitters now track the expression result separately from the stored word, the invariant emitStoreLocal already kept. The float branch returns its DOUBLE register rather than an i64, since coercing first would hand box_float an integer bit pattern

an UNHINTED static property holding a FLOAT reads back as a garbage int: `public static $f = 0.0; M::$f = 2.5; var_dump(M::$f)` answers int(4612811918334230528) where php answers float(2.5). The store boxes, because the declared type is KIND_UNKNOWN and that is inside the boxing condition, so the slot correctly holds box_float(2.5). But in this NaN-boxing scheme a plain double IS its own encoding — 2.5 is 0x4004000000000000, outside the NaN tag space — and the UNKNOWN read path emits a runtime guard that tests for the tag and, failing it, calls box_int on the raw word. "Not tagged" is ambiguous there: it means either a raw int or a double, and the adapter resolves it to INT unconditionally. A `float` hint and a `mixed` hint are both correct, so only the erased channel diverges. Found while measuring the assign-as-expression repro matrix and confirmed in statement position with no value-position involved, which is why it is a separate row. Silent, no crash

lane (b) had never produced a single stub list, and the reason was mechanical: run_tier.sh wrote the generated manifest to the PROBE root and built from there, while composer.json, vendor/ and the generated tiers/ entry all live under app/. `entry: tiers/tN_smoke.php` resolved to a file that was never there and the build died before the link stage every time. Manifest and cwd are now both the app root

a manifest `exclude` written `./src` silently matched NOTHING for the project's own autoload roots, while the identical spelling worked for every vendor package. composer_path_join drops a `.` base, so a vendor root arrives as ./vendor/name/src but the project's arrives as bare src, and the exclude was a raw str_starts_with. Every tier was therefore compiling the whole application: T1 failed on Command::SUCCESS, a T4 construct. exclude_matches() now normalises a leading ./ on both sides. Not audit-only — any user excluding their own directory was being ignored

./var (the warmed cache: dumped DI container, compiled templates) is an APPLICATION artifact referencing every tier, and it was not in the non-T8 exclusion list beside ./src and ./config — so it put the whole app back into every tier

a top-level `return` NESTED IN AN `if` inside any non-entry file terminates the WHOLE PROGRAM, so the entry never runs and the binary silently does nothing (rc 0, no output). lower_module flattens every file top-level statements into one __main with the entry last, and deliberately drops a non-entry file top-level `return` so an include-return cannot end the program - but that drop only recognises a `return` that IS a top-level statement, and one nested in an `if` survives the flatten. The shape is composer own, not contrived: vendor/autoload.php returns the loader, and every symfony polyfill bootstrap is a version-guarded `return require`. THIS IS WHY THE FIRST LINKING T1 RUN PRODUCED AN EMPTY STUB LIST: with main empty the whole module is dead-code-eliminated, so the tier reads as complete while having measured nothing - exactly the failure README.md predicted and the smoke entry exists to prevent. Verified PRE-EXISTING with a non-foldable condition, so it is not a regression from the guard-folding work. Fixing it wants each non-entry file top-level statements in their own scope, i.e. the lazy per-file unit model already recorded under include-once-repeat-not-tracked

a file covered by two composer autoload roots was compiled TWICE and clang rejected the module with an invalid redefinition of the stub class constructor. symfony polyfills map psr-4 to the PACKAGE ROOT and then classmap a subdirectory of it, and the existing guard compared directory STRINGS, so a nested root was never equal to its parent. Deduped by FILE PATH instead, which is robust to any overlap. Not audit-only: any project whose autoload roots nest hits it

composer autoload.exclude-from-classmap was ignored, so shipped-but-excluded code was compiled. 51 of the 99 packages in the corpus declare it, almost always /Test/ or /Tests/, and those directories hold PHPUnit test-case base classes whose parent is a DEV dependency that --no-dev never installs: symfony/service-contracts ServiceLocatorTestCase extends TestCase and the tier-1 module failed on an undefined assertFalse. Now honoured, scoped to the package that declared it - one package saying /Test/ says nothing about another, and over-exclusion is a regression exactly as over-inclusion is

a define guarded by if-not-defined never registered the constant, so a later bareword reference was a hard MIR.lower unknown-constant error. That is THE polyfill idiom - 45 guarded defines across the tier-1 packages, every one with this exact shape and not a version conditional among them - and it reached lowering through a DEFAULT PARAMETER VALUE, which must be a compile-time constant. It blocked 9 of 21 tier-1 packages, i.e. the entire polyfill layer. Only this shape is admitted and only for the SAME name the guard tests, which is what makes it sound without evaluating anything: the constant world is closed at compile time, so "nobody else defined N" is decidable. An unconditional define still wins and a duplicate never overwrites - which is also what makes the case that actually occurs harmless, a polyfill shipping both bootstrap.php and bootstrap80.php with whole-program AOT compiling both

foldGuard folded strict equality between compile-time constants but not ORDERED comparisons, so a PHP_VERSION_ID range guard stayed a runtime branch and its body was lowered. Those bodies DECLARE CLASSES, which lowering does not support as a statement, so tier 1 died on "unsupported statement kind Class" inside the polyfill-php85 NoDiscard stub. Folding is also the only correct answer - this compiler targets 8.5, so the shim must not exist and declaring it anyway would shadow the real thing. Deliberately not routed through a nullable-int helper: a nullable scalar null does not read back as null under the self-host, the same trap the tri-state guard encoding exists for, so the operands stay as the tagged string keys constScalarKey already produces

preallocateLocals was a hand-written list of node kinds, and a kind missing from it is not a missed optimisation but INVALID IR: the local StoreLocal emits a store with an EMPTY pointer operand and clang rejects the module with "expected instruction opcode", pointing at the following line. An assignment inside an isset() subscript in symfony/polyfill-intl-messageformatter was one such kind; a static call args had already been patched the same way earlier, one bug at a time. Every kind not special-cased now recurses over its children generically, so the walk is exhaustive by construction. Safe against the one case that would be wrong: Walk::children of a CLOSURE yields its captures, never its body, so a StoreLocal belonging to a nested frame cannot take a slot in this one
